architecture.mechanism: A heated liquid is drawn from a reservoir, supplied into wind turbine blades, and dispersed within their internal structure so that conducted heat melts accreted ice.
architecture.intervention: Install a closed-loop heated-liquid circuit inside the offshore blade: corrosion-resistant (duplex stainless or polymer-lined) channels bonded to the spar/shell, a reservoir plus heater and pump in the hub/nacelle, and a salt-sealed rotary coupling; thermostatically cycle the fluid so heat conducts outward through the shell to melt the ice layer at the leading edge.
architecture.expected_effect: Ice adhesion fails and accreted ice sheds from the rotating blade, restoring the clean aerodynamic profile and winter power output, with no externally exposed heaters or coatings to be eroded by salt spray and high winds.
architecture.falsification_test: In a climatic wind tunnel, accrete glaze ice on a blade section at -10 C with salt-spray preconditioning, run the internal heated-liquid loop at 25 m/s wind, and log ice-shed time, surface temperature distribution, and post-test fluid leakage/corrosion after 100 salt-fog cycles versus an unheated control.

challenge.kill_reason: all checks passed: evidence verified, no specific disclosure, adversarial survived, falsification concrete
